run_metadata.coverage_summary: Degraded, SEARCH-ONLY run. The hard egress constraint seen on recent runs persisted: the session network policy denied all direct HTTPS to tender hosts. WebFetch returned DNS ENOTFOUND for www.tenders.gov.au (and the same failure mode applies to the other buyer portals), so per environment guidance no further direct fetches were attempted. No buyer-originated portal, detail page, feed/API or tender document could be opened; discovery was limited to the WebSearch tool (US-indexed, returning mostly cached snapshots and third-party aggregator pages). Tier 1 (AusTender; NSW buy.nsw; VIC Buying for Victoria; QLD Brisbane/Cairns; WA/SA/TAS; NT QTOL; ACT) swept by search only. Tier 2 (local government via VendorPanel and council sites; universities/TAFEs; water corporations and other GBEs; ports/airports; public health) checked by search; several confirmable buyer-originated local-government opportunities with reference numbers and closing dates were surfaced and are carried at headline level (UNVERIFIED on the buyer page, see notes). Tier 3 (SAP Ariba Discovery/Business Network; BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue/Woodside; NBN Co/Australia Post/Transgrid; major retail/bank/telco/utility supplier portals; EstimateOne construction) checked by search - every corporate channel remained registration-gated or invitation-only with no publicly-visible open RFx; recorded as portals only, none fabricated. One high-value, well-corroborated corporate opportunity (Sydney Airport architectural & engineering consultant panel for its ~$6bn five-year capital works program) was surfaced from multiple trade/industry outlets and carried at headline level. The known carryover NSW Government Master Media tender (closing 27 Nov 2026) was re-asserted as closing-soon under its existing dedup_key. The University of Notre Dame Australia 'RFT: Insurance Brokerage Services' listing was investigated and found STALE (deadline 12 April 2024) - excluded, not captured. No opportunity, deliverable, date, value or contact was fabricated; every captured item is flagged as headline-only pending a detail pass that requires egress to be restored.
gaps: HARD EGRESS BLOCK: all direct HTTPS to tender hosts denied by the session network policy (WebFetch DNS ENOTFOUND - hosts outside allowed domains). This has blocked full discovery on multiple consecutive runs. To restore full discovery, at minimum these hosts should be allowed in the session network settings: www.tenders.gov.au, buy.nsw.gov.au and www.tenders.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au / supply.qld.gov.au, www.tenders.wa.gov.au, www.tenders.sa.gov.au, www.tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, www.tenders.act.gov.au, www.vendorpanel.com.au, service.ariba.com, www.brisbane.qld.gov.au, estimateone.com, and individual council/university/utility/corporate sites.

Every tender captured this run is headline-only and UNVERIFIED on the buyer's own page: the reference numbers, titles and closing dates come from WebSearch snippets of aggregator and buyer pages, but the buyer detail pages and tender documents could not be opened (egress block). Deliverables, requirements, eligibility, evaluation criteria, submission mechanics, value and contacts are therefore null and still need a detail pass.

Tier 3 corporate (SAP Ariba Discovery, BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue, Woodside, NBN Co, Australia Post, Transgrid, Woolworths, Coles, Qantas, major banks/telcos) remained registration-gated or invitation-only; no authenticated supplier session is available, so no corporate opportunity could be read. Recorded as portals only; no corporate tender fabricated. The Sydney Airport consultant panel is the one corporate item carried, sourced from trade/industry press, not an opened buyer page.

Excluded / not fabricated: University of Notre Dame Australia 'RFT: Insurance Brokerage Services' appeared 'OPEN' on the UNDA supplier page but the linked detail shows a deadline of 17:00 WST 12 April 2024 - a stale listing, not a current opportunity; excluded. Various aggregator snippets (globaltenders, bidsfactory, projectory, tenderhub) with unattributed buyers or passed closing dates were used only as discovery signals and not captured as opportunities.

WebSearch is US-indexed and returned predominantly stale or aggregator data; genuinely recent (last 24-48h) buyer-originated notices are almost certainly undercounted this run. Publish dates for the captured council tenders could not be confirmed (null) - recency is inferred only from early-to-mid December 2026 closing dates.
recommended_seed_additions: Cairns Regional Council (QLD) - https://www.cairns.qld.gov.au/council/tenders/anticipated - buyer-originated 'Anticipated procurement' forward-pipeline page; useful for early market signals; not previously in the known-source set.

Energy Networks Australia (industry body) - https://www.energynetworks.com.au/miscellaneous/notices/ - member electricity/gas network notices board; low confidence as a buyer-originated portal but a good DISCOVERY SIGNAL to find network/utility buyers (Ausgrid, Transgrid, Western Power, Powerlink, etc.) to pivot to their own supplier pages.
Sydney Airport corporate procurement / consultant panel channel - confirm Sydney Airport's own supplier/procurement page and capture the architectural & engineering panel EOI once egress is restored.
